content:
alex: Heads up — started seeing a cluster-wide latency tail and intermittent 503s from eu-west around 09:12 UTC. Many requests auto-fell back to us-east and customers report +180ms RTT. Also noticed unexpected billing bump for a subset of keys. Anyone on call?
maria: I can take a look. Which customers/keys? any repro?
alex: Customer request_id=cli-9a7f; examples in logs: `route_decision=spillover -> us-east (policy=auto, reason=capacity_exhausted, shard=eu-west-hot-12)`
kevin: tagging in @maria @anjali. This looks like the new spillover fanout policy kicked in when hotshard queues hit 95%. We did enable multi-region fallback for this tenant last week.
anjali: @alex can you paste a minimal curl that reproduces? we should verify whether tokens are getting exchanged twice (billing).
alex: repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_KEY" \ 
  -d '{"model":"xlarge-v1","input":"test latency"}'
```
Sending 500 rps for ~30s reproduces the tail locally.
billing-bot: NOTE: account acct-332 reported 12% increase in token usage at 09:14 UTC (auto-alert).
sre-bot: Alert: eu-west shard queue depth exceeded high-water threshold (95%). Automatic spillover engaged to fallback region: us-east.
maria: Ok seeing the same in logs: `fallback_decision: policy=auto_spillover, targets=[us-east,ap-south], chosen=us-east, fallback_reason=queue_backpressure`. Any 401/403s seen?
alex: No auth errors on these traces. But a subset of requests show duplicated trace IDs after routing, e.g., `traceid=tr-019a` appears twice with two different region tags. Could cause duplicate billing if we double-emit tokens.
kevin: That duplication sounds like the proxy retry + fallback path both executing token ledger increment. We changed ledger behavior for retries in the last release. @maria can you grep for `ledger.increment` around those traceids?
maria: grep shows: `ledger.increment(traceid=tr-019a, amount=214) -> successfully emitted` then later `fallback_exec( traceid=tr-019a ) -> ledger.increment(amount=214)`. So yes, double-increment.
anjali: Ugh. So two problems: (1) spillover is aggressive and routing is causing cross-region latency, (2) billing double-count on fallback path. Need mitigation ASAP.
kevin: Short-term mitigation: disable auto_spillover for eu-west-tenants with high-cost keys, set policy to soft-queue (return 429 instead of spillover) while we patch ledger. Also add idempotency guard on ledger.increment keyed by traceid.
anjali: I can roll a policy change now. @kevin can you open a hotfix PR for idempotent ledger? put rollback knob.
kevin: opening PR now — will include feature flag `ledger.idempotency.v1`.
kevin: PR 4521 created: `fix(ledger): de-dupe increments by traceid for fallback paths`. CI running.
support-ops: Noting impacted customers: acct-332, acct-990, acct-114. I've queued outreach and credits pending root cause.
billing-bot: Draft credit: 10% token credit for window 09:12-09:28 for affected accounts.
maria: For repro notes — sequence to reproduce: 1) pin a client to eu-west, 2) ramp to 400-600 rps sustained, 3) observe queue depth on hot shard eu-west-hot-12 reach >90%, 4) automatic spillover picks us-east, 5) proxy executes fallback path causing second ledger increment.
alex: Additional datapoint — some customers reported 401s during the spillover window. I found entries like `auth.fail: token_scope_mismatch` around 09:15 but those correlate with requests that were routed to a different region where the token was scoped to eu-west only. So cross-region fallback broke scope assumptions.
kevin: We need to ensure fallbacks only route to regions compatible with token scope. Add check in routing decision: `if token_scope != target_region then skip target`. I'll add to PR.
maria: For immediate triage: (A) policy change to disable auto spillover for eu-west (anjali to apply), (B) rollback ledger change if PR can't merge quickly, (C) manual credits for affected customers (support-ops).
anjali: Applying policy change now: `PATCH /config/policies/eu-west` -> set `spillover.enabled=false` for tenancy-group high-cost. Patch applied at 09:36 UTC.
anjali: After patch, queue tail reduced and fallback events stop within ~30s. Observed latency back to normal.
kevin: CI passed for ledger idempotency PR. Merging to canary channel now. Canary rollout scheduled to eu-west-proxies only.
kevin: Merged and rolled to canary at 10:02 UTC. Metrics: duplicate ledger events dropped for traceids seen in canary by 98%.
maria: Monitoring: no further billing spikes observed post-canary; waiting for full rollout.
support-ops: Outreach sent to impacted customers with explanation and provisional credit.
kevin: Follow-ups: (1) add token-scope guard in routing (PR 4522), (2) add unit test for fallback ledger idempotency, (3) postmortem with timeline + RCA.
alex: Thanks all. Please add the customer repro package and logs to the incident folder.
maria: Will create postmortem draft and ping for review. :thumbsup:
kevin: I'll add the config knob to avoid abrupt spillovers during hotshard events (config param `spillover.max_rate_per_shard`).
anjali: Closing loop here — service stabilized after policy patch + canary fix. Leaving this thread open for postmortem edits.
